bib.title: A-Mem: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents

question: Can an LLM agent memory that builds linked, self-updating Zettelkasten-style notes outperform fixed-structure memory systems on long-term conversational QA?
hypothesis: Dynamic note construction, link generation and memory evolution give better organised memory than predefined schemas and fixed workflows.
contributions: A-MEM, an agentic memory system with autonomous generation of contextual descriptions, dynamic connections and evolution of existing memories.
Update mechanism where a new memory triggers link generation and memory evolution.
Evaluation on LoCoMo across six foundation models and six metrics, plus t-SNE visualisations.

method.summary: Each interaction becomes a note (content, timestamp, LLM-written keywords, tags, context, embedding, links). On insertion the top-k cosine neighbours are fetched, an LLM decides links, and an LLM may rewrite neighbours' context, keywords and tags. Retrieval is top-k cosine over note embeddings. No training; prompts only.
method.task: long-term conversational question answering with agent memory

evidence.quote: we primarily employ k=10 for top-k memory selection to maintain computational efficiency, while adjusting this parameter for specific categories to optimize performance

results.claim: Removing both link generation and memory evolution drops GPT-4o-mini multi-hop F1 from 27.02 to 9.65.
results.setup: LoCoMo, GPT-4o-mini, single run, ablation of A-MEM.
results.table: Table 3, row w/o LG & ME, column Multi Hop F1 (A-MEM row: 27.02)

results.claim: Link generation alone (w/o ME) recovers most of the multi-hop F1: 21.35 vs full 27.02.
results.table: Table 3, row w/o ME, column Multi Hop F1

results.claim: On DialSim A-MEM reaches F1 3.45, 35% above LoCoMo (full-context) and 192% above MemGPT.
results.setup: DialSim (~350,000 tokens, 1,300 sessions); LoCoMo and MemGPT as baselines; F1 values are very low in absolute terms.
results.quote: score of 3.45 (a 35% improvement over LoCoMo’s 2.55 and 192% higher than MemGPT’s 1.18)

results.claim: A-MEM uses about 1,200 tokens per memory operation versus about 16,900 for LoCoMo and MemGPT, an 85-93% reduction.
results.setup: LoCoMo QA; tokens counted per question answered.
results.quote: The system requires approximately 1,200 tokens per memory operation, achieving an 85-93% reduction in token usage compared to baseline methods (LoCoMo and MemGPT with 16,900 tokens)

results.claim: With GPT-4o, A-MEM temporal F1 is 39.41 vs 9.09 for LoCoMo (full conversation in prompt), at 1,216 tokens vs 16,910.
results.table: Table 1, row 4o A-MEM, column Temporal F1 (LoCoMo 9.09); Token Length 1,216 vs 16,910

results.claim: With GPT-4o, A-MEM loses to the full-context LoCoMo baseline on single-hop (48.43 vs 61.56 F1) and adversarial (36.35 vs 52.61 F1) questions.
results.table: Table 1, row 4o A-MEM, columns Single Hop F1 48.43 and Adversial F1 36.35; LoCoMo 61.56 and 52.61

results.claim: With GPT-4o-mini, A-MEM multi-hop F1 is 27.02 vs 25.02 (LoCoMo) and 26.65 (MemGPT), a small margin.
results.note: Text of Sec 4.3 says A-MEM achieves 'at least two times better performance' in Multi-Hop for GPT models; Table 1 shows 27.02 vs 25.02 and 26.65 for GPT-4o-mini and 32.86 vs 28.00 and 30.36 for GPT-4o.
results.table: Table 1, row GPT 4o-mini A-MEM, column Multi Hop F1

results.claim: With small open models A-MEM beats all baselines in most cells, e.g. Qwen2.5-1.5b temporal F1 24.32 vs 4.46 best baseline.
results.table: Table 1, row Qwen2.5 1.5b A-MEM, column Temporal F1

results.claim: Each memory operation costs under $0.0003 with commercial APIs.
results.setup: Estimate stated in text, no breakdown given.
results.quote: each memory operation costing less than $0.0003 when using commercial API services

results.claim: Processing takes 5.4 s per operation with GPT-4o-mini and 1.1 s with local Llama 3.2 1B on one GPU.
results.setup: Latency of memory processing; GPU model not given.
results.quote: Processing times average 5.4 seconds using GPT-4o-mini and only 1.1 seconds with locally-hosted Llama 3.2 1B on a single GPU.

results.claim: Retrieval time for A-MEM grows from 0.31 us at 1,000 memories to 3.70 us at 1,000,000, slower than MemoryBank (1.91 us) but vastly faster than ReadAgent (120,069.68 us).
results.setup: Vector retrieval timing over identical memory contents, four scales.
results.quote: Even when scaling to 1 million memories, A-MEM’s retrieval time increases only from 0.31µs to 3.70µs

results.claim: Multi-hop F1 with GPT-4o-mini rises with k then plateaus: 19.91 at k=10, 27.02 at k=40, 26.81 at k=50; adversarial peaks at k=40 (50.03).
results.note: Table 1 headline numbers for GPT models use per-category tuned k (40/40/50/50/40), not k=10; text says 'primarily employ k=10'.
results.table: Figure 3(a) values (read from figure): k=10 19.91, k=40 27.02, k=50 26.81; Table 8 gives k=40 for GPT-4o-mini multi-hop

results.claim: Embeddings of A-MEM notes cluster more coherently than the no-LG/ME base in t-SNE for sampled dialogues.
results.setup: Two dialogues in main text, eight in appendix; qualitative only.
results.quote: A-MEM (shown in blue) consistently exhibits more coherent clustering patterns compared to the baseline system (shown in red)

limits: Quality of organisation depends on the underlying LLM (authors, Sec 6).
Single run per cell, no error bars (checklist).
Only LoCoMo and DialSim, both conversational QA; LoCoMo baseline puts whole conversation in prompt and does better on single-hop and adversarial with GPT-4o.
Text claims 'at least two times better' multi-hop for GPT models but Table 1 margins are small there.
Headline GPT results use per-category tuned k (up to 50) while text says k=10; tuning data not stated.
DialSim absolute scores are very low (F1 3.45).
Retrieval-time microbenchmark measures vector search only, not LLM calls for link generation and evolution.
Venue on PDF is a NeurIPS checklist version, arXiv v11 labelled Preprint.
